title: Listening to reissue records with Jeff Holden, then finding the Sydney Jazz Club
summary: Bull met friends including Jeff Holden who played him reissues of Dodds, Oliver, Bix and George Lewis, and then they went to the Sydney Jazz Club and saw the Paramount Jazz Band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right. Yes, well, as I said, I met Jeff Holden and a few other friends that I used to play tennis with, and I'd known some of them from around the district. The district? Around our district. Well, around our district. Oh, our district. Unfortunately, not this district. Oh, we'd be playing different music. Anyway, he invited me over to his place because I was interested in a bit of jazz, and he played me a few records, and we used to then listen to records regularly. Every second day we'd be somewhere listening to records. And we had a lot of the old reissues of the Johnny Dodds and King Olivers and the blues singers and Tommy Ladner and all that sort of stuff that they reissued. And he also had some white stuff, some of the early white, red niggles and that sort of business.
And that white New Orleans. Oh, well, he had bits and pieces, yeah.

I think he had the Popper Lane record, you know, the Popper Lane's children record and a few of those things. And we used to just sort of collect records. One of the first records I ever got was, and I remember when I got it I thought it was the only copy in existence in the world. I got a Bix record. And I'd read, you know, we used to read a little bit of books and that and then, and there's, you know, all these glorious mysteries that shroud characters like Bix because he was a big hard drinker and died young and all this sort of business. And I got this Bix record and I thought it was the end of the earth, you know. But we used to listen to those records and we also got some George Lewis records, which were just coming out then. Those, also on London, you know, a couple of LPs with Alvin Alcorn and the Quartech on the other side. Mm-hmm. And, and Jazz Aphespas. Now this was all sort of, this was purely in a small clique of our own, if you like to call it a clique. And it was completely oblivious to any jazz scene that was in Sydney. And I didn't even know it existed, but Geoff Halton knew of the Sydney Jazz Club. He'd been there once or twice. So we then decided to go down there. So we went to the Sydney Jazz Club and we, I was quite amazed to see a mob of fellows up on the stage playing this stuff, or a semblance of this stuff. Mm-hmm. I mean, though, at that stage of the game, that's about 19, about 1959. Oh, they weren't young men, there's the fellows in the Paramount Jazz Band and they were in their thirties then. And they were playing this sort of stuff. And I was quite amazed to see these fellows actually up there playing the instruments and doing this sort of thing. What do you mean by this sort of thing, like...? Playing jazz, like, like, I happened to learn I had associated purely with these records.
